```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
  eval = requireNamespace("org.Hs.eg.db", quietly = TRUE)
)
```

RSEM writes one `*.genes.results` file per sample, with genes named by Ensembl
IDs such as `ENSG00000141510.18`. Downstream work usually needs the opposite:
one table, **genes by samples, with gene symbols as row names**.

`rsem_read()` makes that table. It is the only function in rsemverse today.

```{r}
library(rsemverse)

ex <- system.file("extdata", "example", package = "rsemverse")

tpm <- rsem_read(
  data     = file.path(ex, "data"),
  metadata = file.path(ex, "metadata.csv"),
  species  = "human",
  expr     = "tpm"
)
head(tpm, 4)
```

The result is an ordinary data frame. Give it any name you like and save it
however you like, for example `write.csv(tpm, "tpm.csv")`.

## What you need

Two things: a folder of RSEM files and a small CSV that lists them.

```text
metadata.csv
data/
  S1.genes.results
  S2.genes.results
  S3.genes.results
```

`metadata.csv` has two columns, `sample_id` and `ref`. `ref` is the name of the
sample's file inside `data`:

```{r, echo = FALSE, comment = ""}
cat(readLines(file.path(ex, "metadata.csv")), sep = "\n")
```

Any other columns are ignored, and the columns of the result follow the order
of the rows in this file.

## The four arguments

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `"data"` | folder that contains the RSEM files |
| `metadata` | `"metadata.csv"` | the CSV above |
| `species` | none, required | `"human"` or `"mouse"` |
| `expr` | none, required | `"count"` (RSEM `expected_count`) or `"tpm"` (RSEM `TPM`) |

`species` and `expr` have no default on purpose. A wrong species would leave
every gene without a symbol, so the function asks you to say which one you
mean, and it stops if the gene IDs belong to the other species.

## What happens to the genes

1. The version of each Ensembl ID is removed (`ENSG00000141510.18` becomes
   `ENSG00000141510`) and the gene symbol is looked up in `org.Hs.eg.db`
   (human) or `org.Mm.eg.db` (mouse).
2. Rows that end up with the same symbol are **added together**.
3. A gene without a symbol keeps the `gene_id` from your file, so nothing is
   dropped and every column adds up to exactly what it did in the input.

A message tells you how many genes fell into each group:

```{r, echo = FALSE}
invisible(rsem_read(file.path(ex, "data"), file.path(ex, "metadata.csv"),
                    species = "human", expr = "count"))
```

The chunk above is the same call with `expr = "count"`. Every number in that
message is explained in [How it works](how-it-works.html).
